blocks.text: How can we make informed guesses about a population's characteristics from a small sample? This is the essence of statistical estimation.

blocks.markdown: In statistics, estimation is about using sample data to infer the properties of an unknown population parameter. This process involves two main types of estimates: point estimates and interval estimates.

blocks.title: Point Estimate
blocks.text: A point estimate is a single value that serves as an estimate of a population parameter. For example, the sample mean \( \bar{x} \) is a point estimate of the population mean \( \mu \).

blocks.markdown: While point estimates provide a specific value, they do not convey any information about the uncertainty or variability of the estimate. This is where interval estimation comes into play.

blocks.title: Interval Estimate
blocks.text: An interval estimate provides a range of values, called a confidence interval, that is likely to contain the population parameter. It is expressed with a certain level of confidence, such as 95%.

blocks.markdown: To construct a confidence interval, we need to understand the concept of standard error, which measures the variability of a point estimate.

blocks.title: Standard Error
blocks.text: The standard error of a statistic is the standard deviation of its sampling distribution. For the sample mean, it is calculated as \( \text{SE}(\bar{x}) = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} \), where \( s \) is the sample standard deviation and \( n \) is the sample size.

blocks.title: Calculating a Point Estimate and Standard Error
blocks.prompt: Given a sample data set: [5, 7, 8, 6, 9], calculate the sample mean and its standard error.

blocks.markdown: Now that we have the standard error, we can construct a confidence interval for the population mean.

blocks.title: Constructing a 95% Confidence Interval
blocks.prompt: Using the sample mean and standard error from the previous example, construct a 95% confidence interval for the population mean.

blocks.answer: The 95% confidence interval for the population mean is (5.61, 8.39).

blocks.title: Interpreting Confidence Intervals
blocks.text: A 95% confidence interval means that if we were to take many samples and build a confidence interval from each, approximately 95% of those intervals would contain the true population mean.

blocks.markdown: It's crucial to understand what a confidence interval does not mean. It does not imply that there is a 95% probability that the true parameter is within the interval for a given sample.

points: Point estimates provide a single value to estimate a population parameter.
Confidence intervals give a range of values that likely contain the parameter, with a specified level of confidence.
The standard error is key to constructing confidence intervals.
